notes: Access: same blocking pattern as the Bestsellers/New-Arrivals files for this company -- direct HTTP and headless Playwright both hard-blocked (403 Access Denied, Akamai) on every macys.com URL, so used Claude-in-Chrome as last resort after confirming robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. SALE-VS-CLEARANCE REASONING: the Home department's 'Sale & Clearance' mega-menu link (/shop/sale/by-category/home?id=24294) resolves to a page titled 'Home Sale | Deals on Bedding, Furniture, Decor & More', breadcrumb Sale > Shop by Category > Home, heading 'Home Sale (500+)', where essentially every product tile is tagged 'Limited-Time Special' -- this is a generic, temporary promotional-sale hub (1,883 pages of results spanning ordinary discounted merchandise), so per the brief's strict test it was EXCLUDED as Clearance. The site does separately expose a genuine Clearance taxonomy: the 'Up to 70% off clearance' Today's Deals banner (marketing copy) actually redirects to the generic site-wide '/shop/sale?id=3536' Sale hub, not a clearance page -- also excluded as a link source. However that Sale hub's own facet list includes a 'Clearance' link (distinct id=54698) leading to '/shop/sale/clearance-closeout?id=54698', titled 'Clearance Sale | Shop Top Brands & Markdowns', breadcrumb Sale > Clearance -- a real, separately-labeled clearance taxonomy node (not just a filter on the generic Sale page), where product tiles are individually tagged 'Clearance' rather than 'Limited-Time Special'. This node exposes a 'Home' department filter leading to the Home-scoped listing used below: '/shop/sale/clearance-closeout/home?id=54710', titled 'Home | Clearance | Sale | Macy's', breadcrumb Sale > Clearance > Home, heading 'Home - Clearance & Closeout (500+)'. This satisfies the brief's test: the site's own taxonomy (breadcrumb + title + per-product 'Clearance' tag) treats it as permanent-markdown/closeout merchandising, distinct from the ordinary 'Home Sale' promotional hub. QTY: the header shows a capped '(500+)', not an exact figure. Sampled the last two pages via unique '/shop/product/' link counts: page 33 of 34 returned 60 unique product links and page 34 (last) returned 38, which would give a computed total of 33*60+38=2,018 IF every one of pages 1-32 also holds exactly 60. That per-page-uniformity assumption could not be safely relied on: an identical sampling check on the Bestsellers PLP for this same company found page 6 of 7 returned 61 unique product links rather than a clean 60 (likely sponsored/ad-tile variance), so page counts on this platform are not guaranteed uniform. Per the qty rule's explicit ban on estimating/aggregating a count, qty was left null; the computed 2,018 figure is recorded in the flag for the reviewer's benefit only, not asserted as fact. No genuine Clearance sub-structure (e.g. 'Furniture Clearance', 'Bed & Bath Clearance' as distinct labeled child listings) was found -- the department chips shown (Bed & Bath, Kitchen & Dining, Furniture, Luggage & Backpacks, Mattresses, Home Decor) link to each department's own general landing page, not to clearance-scoped children, so a single row was emitted.

rows.evidence: Page heading text 'Home - Clearance & Closeout (500+)' (breadcrumb Sale > Clearance > Home; products individually tagged 'Clearance') -- an explicitly capped, non-exact display; pagination runs '1 ... 30 31 32 33 34'
rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: exact qty not obtainable -- site caps the displayed count at '500+'; counting unique product links on the last two of 34 pages (60 on page 33, 38 on page 34) suggests a total near 2,018, but per-page counts on this platform were shown not to be perfectly uniform (a sibling Bestsellers page returned 61 links on one page instead of 60), so this computed figure is not asserted as the verified exact total
